question: Before implementing another dependency-closure generator, does the same source-derived value/state expansion have real input paths and produce something outside existing constructors?
definition: A uniquely resolved producer method returns an expression that MAY read a receiver field; that result reaches a consumer argument inline or through a directly checked local definition, with a frontend link to an observation. Existing source calls contain a writer to the same declaration owner and field. Context/binding uncertainty remains explicit; index compatibility is not solved.

shapes: durability_test.go:106-113: b.Set twice; d.Apply(b, Sync); seqNum=b.SeqNum(); b.Close(); d.WaitForDurability(seqNum)
direct_operation_edges.duplicate_note: The durability chain occurs once in the original source plus five existing trajectory-derived source variants. Seven edges are not seven independent tasks or new combinations.

independent_existing_capability_check.finding: For all six durability source instances, existing producer_contexts already finds one producer port, accepts a nine-statement source slice including state operations, and finds a literal recipient port. Merely calling this a mixed dependency chain does not create a new construction mechanism.

semantic_limit: Matching the same field is too coarse: appending payload bytes to Batch.data need not change the header consumed by SeqNum. Repr also performs a SetCount operation itself. Source MAY dependencies do not prove that an additional writer changes the observation, or that the original test misses a combination.
decision: Do not implement another adapter framework or claim a unified novel abstraction from these counts. Keep the backward value/state expansion idea as an unvalidated hypothesis. A next experiment must first demonstrate a concrete new, relevant construction beyond existing producer/state mechanisms.
